## Summary

The Khmer is strong: short, spoken, and the contrast between Petra (clipped imperatives and nouns) and Hugo (slow formal questions with តើ…ឬ? and បើ…) carries well; every fixed-point pair (ចង់ P49 = P62, bare ឥឡូវ P44 = P57 = P61, ដៃ P43 = P49 = P60, ខាំ P60 = P61, វា for the curse) is intact, the P45/P49 twist reads, and P60–P62 read as a reveal. Three KM lines changed: P30 used bare លា (reads first as "farewell") where spoken Khmer says លាតម្រាមដៃ; P60 gets the object អ្នក so វា can only be the curse biting her, not her hand biting; P29 is an invisible spelling normalisation (ស្ដាំ with subscript ដ, as in ពាក់កណ្ដាល). All other flagged doubts were checked and kept (see Decisions below); no question needs the author. Glossary suggestions for script-editor / continuity-manager: update the P60 full-line memo to «ដៃដដែល… តែមុននេះ វាខាំអ្នក។», record the subscript rule ្ដ (Chuon Nath: ស្ដាំ, កណ្ដាល, បណ្ដាសា), and keep the series title មុនដោះស្រោមដៃ.

## Changes

| Ref | Original KM | Revised KM | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| P29 · 페트라 | ពេត្រា៖ "ដៃស្តាំសិន។" | ពេត្រា៖ "ដៃស្ដាំសិន។" | Same word, dictionary spelling with subscript ដ (្ដ) to match ពាក់កណ្ដាល at P22; it looks identical on screen. |
| P30 · 페트라 | ពេត្រា៖ "លាម្រាមដៃ។" | ពេត្រា៖ "លាតម្រាមដៃ។" | លាត is the everyday verb for spreading the fingers; bare លា reads first as "say goodbye". |
| P60 · 휴고 | ហ៊ូហ្គោ៖ "ដៃដដែល… តែមុននេះ វាខាំ។" | ហ៊ូហ្គោ៖ "ដៃដដែល… តែមុននេះ វាខាំអ្នក។" | Without an object វា could be read as the hand biting; «វាខាំអ្នក» makes it the curse biting her, still only what he saw (P61 keeps ខាំ). |

## Decisions on the flagged doubts (for the human native check)

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| ខាំ for the curse (P60, P61) | Kept. Figurative "bite" for something that nips the skin is natural and gives the nameless វា a creature-like will; ស៊ី ("eat away") would suggest slow spreading, not the momentary nip at the fingertip. |
| វា at P60 | Was ambiguous (nearest noun ដៃ). Fixed with «វាខាំអ្នក»; P31 «វា…» already set វា = the curse. |
| P62 «អ្នកចង់ស្រាប់ហើយឬ?» | Kept. ស្រាប់ហើយ ("already, from before") is natural speech and marks the past with តាំងពីដំបូង; bare «ចង់ហើយឬ?» can read "you want it now?". Bare ចង់ works as an open question and is not narrowed to lust; ឬ leaves it open. |
| លោកម្ចាស់ for a count (P14, P27) | Kept. It is what Khmer dubs and translations use for a servant's lord or master; ឯកឧត្តម sounds like a modern official. As Petra's only address, after «ចិត្តល្អម្ល៉េះ», it reads as sarcasm. |
| P2 «រោយ… រោយ…» | Kept. It is a mimetic word (petals dropping) rather than a sound, soft and fitting the quiet ritual. No common Khmer comic sound for crumbling ash comes to mind; a human may prefer a true onomatopoeia. |
| P26 «…យប់នោះឯង អ្នកនឹងចាកចេញ។» | Kept. With the subject អ្នក and the future នឹង it is an indicative statement ("you will leave"), not an imperative (that would be «ចាកចេញទៅ» or «អ្នកត្រូវចាកចេញ»). After «…បានទេ?» and «បើ…» it reads as the proposed clause. |
| Ending caption «— នៅមានតក្នុងភាគទី ២ —» | Kept: correct, and it is the harness standard wording (no added space). |
| Series title | Recommend មុនដោះស្រោមដៃ (short; មុន + verb like មុនដេក). ដោះស្រោមដៃ is a fixed verb phrase, so the colloquial noun ដោះ ("breast") does not surface. The mild "undressing" undertone is the intended sensual layer. មុនពេលដោះស្រោមដៃ is also correct, just longer. |
| ពេត្រា / ហ៊ូហ្គោ | No problem. ត្រា ("seal") is harmless and even fits her wax-thimble seal; ពេត្រុស (Peter) makes ពេ-ត្រ- familiar. ហ្គោ is not read as គោ ("cow"). |
| P23 ខ្ញុំ, P5 ថយទៅ, P16, P20, P24, P34, P38 «មើលទេ?», P39, P43 ខូច, P48, P49, P53, P9 វិមាន, P8 កុម្ម៉ង់, P32 រដូវរងា | Kept as written: natural and faithful. P43 «ធ្វើឲ្យ…ខូច» (caused the damage) is better than បំផ្លាញ, which would imply deliberate destruction. P38 «មើលទេ?» is casual but short like 보겠소?, and ចង់ is reserved for P49/P62. |
| Culture (twist-plan §2-6) | For a human: a woman taking a noble's bare hand first reads as very bold, and looking a superior in the eye reads as defiant. Both suit P17–P19, but the "attraction" layer must come from the drawn blush and lingering eyes. |
